parties: <cite index="1-1,46-1">Reliance Brands Limited (RBL) and SKIMS Body, Inc.</cite>
headline: <cite index="46-1">Reliance Brands and SKIMS announce exclusive partnership to bring the shapewear and lifestyle brand to India</cite>
sum: Reliance Brands Ltd. has entered into an exclusive partnership with global shapewear and apparel brand SKIMS to introduce the label in India, with its first retail stores scheduled to open in Delhi and Mumbai as part of a phased expansion across physical and digital channels. SKIMS marks Kim Kardashian's flagship lifestyle brand entry into the Indian premium consumer market.
implication: Exclusive distribution partnerships for foreign fashion/apparel brands in India typically require careful drafting of territorial rights, local operating covenants, e-commerce carve-outs and IP licensing mechanics-the transaction's multi-channel (store + digital) rollout structure signals negotiation around online exclusivity and channel control in a market where digital-first luxury retail is competing with flagship stores.
detail: <cite index="1-3">Founded in 2019 by Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede, SKIMS offers a range of women's underwear, shapewear, loungewear and menswear, with a focus on fit, comfort and technical innovation.</cite> <cite index="1-4">Under the agreement, Reliance Brands will oversee SKIMS' operations in India across retail and e-commerce, leveraging its extensive portfolio of international fashion and lifestyle brands.</cite> <cite index="1-2">The partnership marks SKIMS' entry into the Indian market and forms part of the brand's ongoing international expansion following recent retail launches in London and Dubai.</cite>

framework.note: General law governing the exclusive partnership agreement; formation, consideration, discharge of obligations.
Regulation of trademark use, labeling and origin marking for imported apparel and consumer goods.
Registration, use and enforcement of SKIMS trademark in India; likely co-branded or licensed mark registration.
Protection of design rights and visual IP in clothing designs; relevant for SKIMS' shapewear designs and marketing materials.

framework.ref: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Contract and Tort provisions)
framework.note: Updated criminal and civil law framework governing breach of exclusive distribution covenants.
Tariff classification and duties on imported apparel (shapewear, loungewear, menswear); applies to initial inventory inflow.
GST classification of apparel and fashion goods (18% slab typical); registration of RBL as GST liable entity for SKIMS sales.

framework.ref: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 & Foreign Investments in India (Promotion & Regulation) Act, 2022
framework.note: Scrutiny of capital flows, FDI limits on retail and brand ownership; SKIMS Inc. is US-domiciled but partnership is asset-light (distribution, not equity JV).
Warranties, product liability, unfair contract terms in sale of SKIMS goods; RBL liable as retailer/e-commerce operator.

conditions: <cite index="46-2">RBL will operate the brand in the country across physical and digital channels</cite>
<cite index="46-2">Opening of first SKIMS stores in India, beginning with Delhi and Mumbai</cite>
Exclusive partnership (SKIMS grants RBL sole right to operate in India)
approvals: Reliance Industries / Reliance Retail Ventures internal approvals (retail policy)
Customs tariff clearance for imported inventory
GST registration for RBL as operator
Store lease/real estate approvals (Delhi & Mumbai flagship locations)
structure.novel: Multi-channel (physical flagships + digital e-commerce) exclusivity structure for US fashion brand in India; celebrity-founder brand (Kim Kardashian) entering India with Reliance's established retail distribution muscle rather than standalone FDI or JV.

triggers.note: Exclusive license to use SKIMS mark; potential co-brandmarks or sub-license terms; assignment/sublicense restrictions.
Tariff duty on imported finished goods and raw materials (if any in-country manufacturing planned); classification as apparel subject to prevailing MFN and preferential trade rates.
RBL's warranties and disclaimers on SKIMS products; product liability indemnity from SKIMS Inc.; handling of defective/counterfeit goods.
e-commerce operator GST registration; ITC eligibility on inventory purchases; cross-border B2B supplies (if SKIMS Inc. exports goods directly to RBL).
Breach of exclusivity; specific performance/injunction remedies; arbitration clause likely drafted under Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996.
